body: Fear Effect is Kronos Digital Entertainment's PlayStation action-adventure, first released in North America on 24 February 2000. Set in Hong Kong in 2050, it follows Hana, Glas and Deke through a story that moves from criminal intrigue towards supernatural horror. The player alternates between its protagonists, combining exploration, combat and puzzles. Its illustrated characters stand against moving backgrounds, giving the scenes a distinctive animated appearance. The presentation makes each location feel like part of a continuous film while the player remains responsible for finding a route through its dangers.

Fear Effect uses streaming or looping full-motion video for its environments rather than relying only on still pre-rendered scenes. Characters move within these animated spaces, where a fixed view can conceal both an object needed for a puzzle and a threat approaching the player. Combat and stealth share time with investigation, making the next scene more than a place to shoot. The player must understand what the camera reveals and what the situation requires. This mixture gives the adventure a deliberate pace, interrupted by sudden demands for action.

The video-based presentation helped spread the original release across four PlayStation discs. Matt Furniss and Jason Agolia supplied its music, while the visual treatment of the characters anticipated techniques that became more common in later games. Reviews generally praised its cinematic character and distinctive appearance, with difficulty a frequent reservation. Fear Effect 2: Retro Helix followed as a prequel in 2001. The original's identity remains closely tied to the contrast between readable, illustrated figures and backgrounds that continue to move around them, supporting a thriller that changes its direction as it unfolds.
